annotation.title_clean: UN Regulation No 171 – Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to Driver Control Assistance Systems (DCAS)
annotation.title_en: UN Regulation No 171 – Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to Driver Control Assistance Systems (DCAS)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: UNECE World Forum for Harmonization of Vehicle Regulations (WP.29), published in the Official Journal of the EU
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union (L series, 2024/2689)
annotation.summary_en: UN Regulation No 171 (published in the EU Official Journal, 2024) sets uniform type-approval requirements for SAE Level 2 Driver Control Assistance Systems in M and N category vehicles. It keeps the driver responsible. It requires driver monitoring, HMI, manoeuvre limits, failure response, audit-based safety assessment, physical and virtual validation, in-service monitoring and reporting, and software identification.
key_provisions_or_claims: DCAS are SAE Level 2 systems; responsibility for driving remains with the driver at all times
Mandatory driver disengagement monitoring (hands-on, eyes-on) with timed warning escalation, ending in a risk mitigation stop
Lane change and manoeuvre constraints: lateral acceleration and jerk limits, deceleration limits for approaching vehicles, 3 s indication
Manufacturers must run in-service monitoring, notify safety-critical occurrences and report annually to the Type Approval Authority
Type approval needs a safety-concept audit, track and road tests, credibility-assessed virtual testing, and compliance with UN R156 software update rules
